SMTO-CTR-0011 — A check found the task plan adds an admin or root login

GUID: 26f4e08d-0169-4d39-9a20-96803619884e
Slug: task-contract-new-credential
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the plan SMTO writes from a request) found it says to log in as root or admin, although the request never asked for that. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reread your request. If you didn't ask SMTO to log in as root or admin, treat this plan as wrong and don't use it. The plan gave itself more powerful access than you asked for.
  2. If the work really needs that access, write it plainly in the request, for example "log in as root". Never type the password itself into the request. Access your request names in those words is allowed in the plan, while passwords should never be written into it.
  3. Send the request again as a new message so SMTO writes a new plan, and keep Task Contract Integrity Guard switched on. A new plan is checked from scratch, and the guard keeps blocking plans that add locations your request didn't include.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, or the new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run a plan that logs in as root or admin unless you asked for that access.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An offline Task Contract check found a root/admin login phrase in the contract's action text that is absent from the accepted source, prior and ingress material.

What this means

  • Offline inspection finds a root/admin login phrase in action text that is absent from accepted source/prior/ingress material. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Offline inspection finds a root/admin login phrase in action text that is absent from accepted source/prior/ingress material.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact credential-role phrase with accepted authority; this is not a password-validity check.

How to fix it

  • validate_contract found a 'login, log in, authenticate or connect as root/admin' phrase in the contract objective, stage objectives or requirement descriptions that does not appear in the source, prior contract or ingress material. Regenerate or correct the contract so it uses only the identity scope the source grants; if elevated access is genuinely needed, state it in the source request and supply credentials only through the supported private credential flow. Keep the Integrity Guard enabled.
  • Remove the unsupported identity addition through the normal contract correction flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The contract describes only accepted identity scope under the supported private credential flow.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the integrity guard as a default fix.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
